heuristics.extrapolation: From 24 full participant-run windows of this program (per-window base ops and evaluated F9 claws in proof.md Appendix C; mean evaluated F9 claws 935.1, s.d. 29.7) and the 4 organizer-run reduced windows (r39k4-window-small) to the attack's 2^82.5423 windows.
heuristics.limitations: Kernel-size conditioning can bias maps and later events; parity shows that the composition preserves that distribution, not that it is uniform. The sample has no all-rejected window, but the true-expectation premise includes them. H1 remains an extrapolation from finite public-seed replays, and forced configurations can cost more.
heuristics.scope: The exact retained first-block filter and r39 walk in experiments/r39joint_k4.py, with 2^26 walk evaluations per accepted window and at most 32 charged attempts.
heuristics.statement: For the retained KCAP=710/KTRY=32 selected-window distribution of the shipped program, the expected charged base-walk work per window is at most 463,618,904 operations (the 99% upper bound over 24 full windows of this program: mean 461,649,658, s.d. 3,858,918; Appendix C), the yield is 58,959.42 groups per window (accepted r39 terms, R39_ACCEPTED_TERMS l.5), and the distinct evaluated F9 claws per distinct claw are at most 0.016203 (99% upper bound over 48 full windows). These are premises on true expectations, priced at their 99% bounds. Claw free words, W17 and the inherited tail must keep the stated uniformity/independence properties after conditioning on selection.

heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory (best case): p_tail = 2^-74.3238, the linear mean of the 14 runs; the replica hard-asserts the conservative check value QDECL = -74.45. The organizer replica experiments/r39tail.py v2 (r39-tail-01..14, 800 particles, variance-balanced stage lanes 8x512/8x2048/8x2048/4x128/6x256/1x4, 20 trials x 80 batches x 2048 proposals = 3,276,800 proposals per run, every particle driving exactly two batches) hard-asserts EXP and verify_smc_stats() on every run: 6,398 verified collisions in 45,875,200 proposals across the 14 public-seed runs, parity classes [1592, 1626, 1624, 1556] (chi-square 2.03 < 7.81). By Del Moral's Feynman-Kac theorem, the unnormalized product estimator Q'_r = 2^(l2_r) * (hits_r / 3276800) is exactly unbiased on the linear scale (E[Q'_r] = Q', zero log-scale Jensen bias): verify_smc_stats() hard-asserts linear-scale mean log2(mean(Q')) = -74.3238, one-sided 99% Student-t lower bound log2(lcb_lin) = -74.3978 > QDECL = -74.45, log-scale 99% bound -74.3987 > -74.45, and the linear one-sided 99.9% bound (t = 3.852, 13 df) -74.4326 > -74.45. QDECL = -74.45 was fixed before the organizer runs by the pre-registered rule (at least 0.01 below the 99.9% bound of the frozen design, rounded down to two decimals); as a one-sided test of the declared value the 14 runs give t = 4.4397 (13 df, p < 1e-3). The v2 program of 0b2616e3 (this replica's code, with the published advice) reproduces 19034ce byte-identically at 19034ce's parameters (three private seed sets: carrier, stage counts, per-trial hits and parity classes identical), so the estimator is unchanged in semantics; only the work allocation changed.
heuristics.limitations: A one-sided 99% confidence lower bound (-74.3978 linear-scale unbiased, -74.3987 log-scale) over 14 organizer-executed replica runs of the Feynman-Kac unbiased estimator, 0.0522 bits above the replica's check value -74.45 (linear 99%; the claim prices the tail at the measured mean -74.3238, best-case premise), and the linear 99.9% bound -74.4326 is 0.0174 above it; the declared value was fixed by a pre-registered rule frozen with the design on private seeds (ten sizing runs, mean -75.4069 sd 0.1235) before any organizer-seed result of this design was seen. Stage 18 is calibrated against direct uniform Monte Carlo (c18 = 206/65536, asserted within 0.0003 of the 14-run SMC stage-18 rate); K_P is a subset of all collision routes so Q <= p_tail. The 14 runs are public-seed replays without a holdout, as in the accepted 4487063; the t-test (t = 4.4397, p < 1e-3) and the pre-registration rule address the coverage finding F-EXP-TAIL-COVERAGE of c30c0d70.
heuristics.scope: The tail rows 18 to 38 of the Table 23 trail after the claw, W8 uniform on F8, W9 uniform on F9, E18..E23 of the first member uniform on 2^32, a0 even and u odd, estimated by the v2 work allocation (800 particles, balanced stage lanes, 3,276,800 proposals per run). Not claimed for another trail or allocation.
heuristics.statement: For the claws of the program (a0 even, u odd, W16 = g, W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98) the probability that the two 39-step compressions of the pair give equal 256-bit outputs (the four parity classes of (a0, u) fall with exact probability 1/4 each; pooling them presumes their exchangeability for the collision event, declared here, and the class-specific estimator 4 * hits_(even, odd) / n, unbiased under that same declared exchangeability premise, is hard-asserted at 99% as -74.4053 > -74.45) is 2^-74.3238, its measured linear mean over the 14 organizer runs (best-case premise; the hard-asserted linear 99.9% bound is -74.4326), for the quantity of proof Section 8 (rows 18 to 38, W18..W23 uniform), a lower bound on the tail probability because the carrier K_P is a subset of all routes to a collision.

heuristics.extrapolation: Trials 0 and 1 of experiment:r39-transplant-claw execute verify_advice_construction() in experiments/r39joint.py: it runs the exact 32-bit bit-by-bit DFS fibre solver solve_row_exact on rows 16 and 17 of the advice pair (verifying g16_fibre_size = 2 with G16 = 0xbca1c321, g17_fibre_size = 1 with W17 = 0x71e9ba98, and fibre_dfs_ops = 1944 < 2812 word operations < 1 target-compression), verifies that steps 9 down to 0 and CV_PUB are uniquely recovered from steps 10 to 15 and W[0..15] by exact downward step inversion with zero search (downward_inv_ok = 1), and enumerates a 256-candidate local slice of the step-15 free bits (advice_slice_cands = 256, advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411 < 4 * 2812 word operations < 2^2 target-compressions). Extrapolated from the 256-candidate slice and the ePrint 2026/1120 Section 4.3 Step 1 measurement (about 2^34.2 SHA-256 calls, Step 2 probability 1) to the 2^34-candidate space on steps 10 to 15.
heuristics.limitations: The fibre, inversion and 256-candidate slice checks do not execute the full 2^34 construction space or the 93-pair campaign. The inherited sequential construction/selection allowance remains 2^43; this revision adds it conservatively to the online bound and does not claim to have verified its full scale or tail-selection premise.
heuristics.scope: One-time offline construction of the 160-byte advice (CV_PUB, M_PUB, MP_PUB) for sha256-r39-prefix-v1; not part of the online walk.
heuristics.statement: H3 (changed from r39): A[8..11], E[12..15], W12..W15 fixed to the published values; A[6] and A[7] range over the 115,010 listed variants; for every listed variant both messages follow the published state-difference trail through step 15 (step-function identity, checked by --k4selftest: base == build, pass == k4_words); at the published point the construction is r39's build exactly.

heuristics.extrapolation: from the measured first stage (W17 hits, cluster sizes) to the unmeasurable tail stage; tail independence across claws is inherited from r39's H5 unchanged.
heuristics.limitations: The tail event (2^-74.3) is priced from the accepted r39 terms, and its cross-claw and within-cluster independence is declared, as in r39's H5; the price counts only distinct passing keys, so it does not use within-cluster tail independence. W17 hit independence is tested only at the 2^-32 stage and only up to the power of 8 events. Claws sharing listed W10 and W11 values share those words; the joint arm tests the marginal tail rate, not joint dependence. This is a proxy, not a proof. Independence in the bulk at rows 19-22 does not imply independence of the 2^-74 tail event.
heuristics.scope: the k4 program experiments/r39joint_k4.py at 2^82.5423 windows (proof.md Section 7); not claimed for another walk.
heuristics.statement: Distinct claws are independent trials for the events "W9 in F9", "some listed variant has W8 in F8 and W17 equal to the published value", and the tail rows 18-38, as in r39 5f8e6192, whose H5 is accepted on the same basis. Every W17 hit is a distinct message pair with its own tail trial. Within a claw hits cluster: entries that share (a2, W10) and pass F8 give the same W17 (measured per F9 claw: 8,072 entries pass F8, 7,621 distinct keys, size-biased mean cluster 1.115, max 4). Cluster mates differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W7 and every tail word from W18 on, so their tails are separate trials (H5 extended, proof.md Section 7). E[H] = G x E[N] x 2^-32 and P(success) = 1 - E[(1 - p_tail)^H], which the program holds at 0.39 with lambda = -ln(0.61) + 2^-40 (Var(H) <= 4 E[H]); the price counts only distinct (a2, W10) keys as trials, so it does not use within-cluster tail independence (proof.md Section 5). Evidence (participant runs with k4pair.c and k4verify.py; proof.md Sections 5, 7, 8): chunk 0 (28 classes) and chunk 1 (13 classes) at 4 CVs each, 134M claws per run, gave 5 W17 hits against about 5.7 expected and 3 against 4.0, all verified and all from distinct claws; the tail joint arm (W8, W10, W11 drawn from 60,000 real k = 4 variant triples, 14 runs) gives a ratio of 2^+0.023, s.d. 0.026. Organizer-run (r39k4-window-small): tail outcomes show no claw-level component. On the hit-conditioned tail (published step-17 state, the lane's own words from W18), the graded distance from the published trail at rows 19-22 has between-claw ANOVA F = 1.27, 0.15, 0.06, 1.24 on 4 trials (528-587 lanes each; p about 0.60 combined; measured by this entry's run and by our run of 9cf5ae57's program on the same seeds). Participant-run on 10 claws and 50,812 lanes: between-claw F <= 1.41 at rows 19-22, ICC <= 0.0001 (k4tailicc.py). This is a graded PROXY for tail independence across claws: rows 19-22 are measured, rows 23-38 are assumed as in r39. Within one claw, cluster mates (same a2, W10) ARE correlated at row 19 (participant-run 0.227); the price therefore counts distinct keys (K4_EN_LB = 128.3032 x 0.942173 = 120.8838) and does not rely on within-cluster independence.

heuristics.extrapolation: from 24 and 48 full participant-run windows to the 2^82.5423 windows of the attack; the per-window work and duplicate rate are properties of one window, measured at full window size.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run window measurements (dedupe_evidence); the organizer-run windows are reduced to 2^21 walk evaluations and check the counted ops exactly through K4_WIN_EXP.
heuristics.scope: the k4 program experiments/r39joint_k4.py with its k4d gate and per-window streamed list; windows of 2^26 walk evaluations as in r39.
heuristics.statement: Declared model constants, each at its own 99% bound (not 99% overall): 2,812 ops per compression (r39 accepted); base walk mu+ = 463,618,904 ops per window (24-window 99% upper bound of this program's measured mean); distinct F9 rate 0.016203 per distinct claw (48-window 99% upper bound; duplicate F9 claws within a window are skipped by the k4d gate); inflate + varint decode charged at 37 ops per raw byte (a counted puff-style decoder measures 36.351); E[N] 128.3032 (16 full first-block CVs, 99% lower bound); key ratio 0.942173 (99% lower bound); tail 74.3238 (r39 accepted); lambda = -ln(0.61) + 2^-40. The program's run cap uses K4_OPS_PER_CLAW = ceil(463,618,904 / 58,959.42 + 251,468 x 0.016203 + 7,322,324 / 58,959.42) = 12,063 (asserted at import), where 251,468 is the pass per F9 claw read back from the asserted K4_WIN_EXP tuples (9cf5ae57: 560,779; this entry tests only W17 in the counted pass and F8 on the scalar words at W17 hits, proof.md Section 3) and 7,322,324 the ops of one list flush; the claimed time is the ceiling of that cap. The cap counts one flush per window: a second flush needs more than K4B = 1,536 distinct F9 claws in one window against a Poisson mean of about 950, probability below 10^-60.

heuristics.extrapolation: from 24 (base walk) and 48 (distinct-F9 rate) full participant-run windows and the 4 organizer-run reduced windows to the attack's window count; uses only independence of windows and the measured per-window variance.
heuristics.limitations: Per-window variance is measured on 24 and 48 full windows; the bound uses Chebyshev only, with no distributional assumption beyond window independence.
heuristics.scope: the shipped program experiments/r39joint_k4.py at B = 2^82.5423 windows of 2^26 walk evaluations, with its own run cap.
heuristics.statement: MODEL with measured inputs. The work cap is reached before B windows complete with negligible probability: the cap per claw (12,063 ops) exceeds the mean work per claw (11,976.88) by 0.719%; the per-window s.d. is at most 12,665,804 (base-walk s.d. over 24 full windows plus the pass s.d. from the 48-window distinct-F9 rate s.d., summed without assuming independence), 1.794% of the window mean; if windows are independent with these moments, the margin is 1.06e+12 s.d. of the total over B = 2^82.5423 windows and Chebyshev bounds the probability below 1e-24. The moments are sample estimates.

heuristics.extrapolation: from a scaled-down event of probability 2^-7 (the full W17 value falling in a hashed target set) to the real event of probability 2^-32 on the same keys.
heuristics.limitations: Organizer-run on 8 claws in 4 reduced windows at the scaled event; the real 2^-32 event is not observable in-window.
heuristics.scope: the shipped program experiments/r39joint_k4.py; W17 events per distinct (a2, W10) key within and across claws and windows.
heuristics.statement: Organizer-run (r39k4-window-small, trials 0-3): a scaled-down event of probability 2^-7, the full W17 value falling in a hashed target set of 2^25 values (the real event with its single target scaled up), counted per distinct (a2, W10) key over 8 claws in 4 windows: 541 hits against 525.7 expected, Pearson 5.74 on 8 dof (p about 0.68). Hits are independent across claws, windows and distinct keys at this scale. A top-bit slice of W17 is NOT used: it is correlated through the shared high bits of the listed a2 values (X² 3,178 on 8 dof, same seeds) and does not model a single-value target.

restrictions: Ordinary collision of SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps from the standard IV, two 64-byte blocks plus the common padding block: the same random first block M0, then M1 vs M1' = M1 + DL with differences in words W8..W12. The second block is the transplanted 2026/1120 Table 23 pair with the two state words A[6] and A[7] released over a listed set of 115,010 variants (proof.md Sections 2.2-2.5), shipped in the program as a compressed literal, sha256-asserted, and stream-decoded once per window flush (never resident as planes). No chaining-value difference. Advice: 2,977 bytes, the 160-byte published pair plus the 2,445-byte encoded list and 372 bytes of class literals.

Credited derivative of Jbenisek's 9cf5ae57 (PR 1657; the k = 4 list, pass, dedupe gate and streamed flush, kept unchanged except that the counted pass tests only W17 and F8 is tested at W17 hits), of newjordan's 3e96c2b6 and of our r39 entry 5f8e6192: the 160-byte published pair, claw search, tail p >= 2^-74.3238 and preprocessing 43 are inherited; the list is built once offline at about 2^24 operations (proof.md Sections 2.5, 8). Peak memory 1,132,453 bytes = 2^20.1110 with every list representation and the two resident literal tables K4_BLOCK_CONST and K4_CLASS_CONST counted (Section 6); success 0.39 (Section 7).
